rounds.proof_sketch: K=4096, TILE_SIZE=32. Loop bound = ceil(4096/32) = 128. Original: t∈[0,127]. Mutated: t∈[0,128]. Extra iteration t=128 has t*TILE_SIZE=4096, so conditions (4096+threadIdx) < 4096 are always false. Both As and Bs are filled with 0.0f. Inner loop computes sum += 0×0 = 0, which doesn't change result.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation adds one extra loop iteration (t=128) to the tiled matrix multiplication. However, with K=4096 exactly divisible by TILE_SIZE=32, the original 128 iterations already perfectly cover all data. In the extra iteration, the boundary conditions (t*TILE_SIZE + threadIdx.x) < K and (t*TILE_SIZE + threadIdx.y) < K both evaluate to (4096 + threadIdx) < 4096, which is always false. This causes both shared memory tiles As and Bs to be filled with zeros. The inner computation then multiplies zeros together, adding exactly 0.0f to every sum. This zero contribution is value-independent and cannot be detected through any input value variation.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed shape contract. The extra iteration always processes zeros due to boundary guards, contributing nothing to the final result. Would require K not divisible by TILE_SIZE to potentially expose the bug.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of tiled GPU kernels, test with dimensions that are NOT exact multiples of the tile size. This would expose off-by-one errors in loop bounds more effectively. The configuration K=4096, TILE_SIZE=32 (exact multiple) masks this class of bugs.
